LanguageData.US.Help.PageTitle.Title: Using This Window
LanguageData.US.Help.PageTitle.Overview: Manage exact voice-pack targets at home. Settings & tools opens your last tool in this window (Behaviour first). Equal-width tabs switch directly; returning keeps your pack, search, target and scroll.
LanguageData.US.Help.PageTitle.Nav.Label: Pages & tools
LanguageData.US.Help.PageTitle.Nav.Text: Voices combines configuration status, mode, volume, search and pack management. Behaviour, presets, output, fallback, appearance, diagnostics and restore are secondary tools, not a permanent sidebar.
LanguageData.US.Help.PageTitle.Apply.Label: Editing and saving
LanguageData.US.Help.PageTitle.Apply.Text: Ordinary edits take effect immediately and save automatically shortly afterwards. Source and action-field edits first attempt saving: failure keeps the previous configuration; saved-but-not-applied changes can be inspected in Diagnostics without saving again. Closing saves applied edits and discards unconfirmed drafts.
LanguageData.US.Help.PageTitle.HelpDrawer.Label: Detailed help & return
LanguageData.US.Help.PageTitle.HelpDrawer.Text: Page help toggles open or closed. It starts with the page overview, then follows real field hover with the exact target. Moving into help holds its last content for reading; the next valid hover replaces it. Hover never reopens closed help. Reopening the same context keeps its reading position; a new target starts at the top. Escape closes inner menus or edits first, then help, then returns from the business page.
LanguageData.US.Help.ModeRow.Title: Routing Mode
LanguageData.US.Help.ModeRow.Overview: Choose how VoicePack audio is routed: Vanilla keeps only the built-in tier, Fallback prefers enabled packs and falls through the tiers in order, Remix draws from the candidates with equal weight, and Disabled bypasses this mod entirely.
LanguageData.US.Help.ModeRow.Vanilla.Text: Uses only the final fallback table for the current race and action; VoicePacks are not routed. US dispatches only when a usable mapping exists and normal response conditions are met. Without a usable mapping, US does not dispatch.
LanguageData.US.Help.ModeRow.Fallback.Text: Short-circuits through the tiers in order: xenotype pack, race pack, pack fallback, then the final fallback table for the current race and action. The final table is tried only when the first three tiers have no usable candidate. If no tier has a usable mapping, US does not dispatch.
LanguageData.US.Help.ModeRow.Remix.Text: Folds every tier's candidates for the domain - xenotype pack, race pack, pack fallback and built-in - into one equally weighted draw pool.
LanguageData.US.Help.ModeRow.Disabled.Text: Bypasses this mod's audio path entirely - no VoicePack and no built-in audio is emitted - pawns behave as the base game defines, and all stored settings are kept.
LanguageData.US.Help.GlobalVolume.Overview: Global volume scales the final loudness of every squeak between 0% and 100%. 0% is not a bypass: selection and modulation still run, only the result is inaudible.
LanguageData.US.Help.GlobalVolume.Slider.Label: Volume Slider
LanguageData.US.Help.GlobalVolume.Slider.Text: Drag to scale all final audio continuously between 0% and 100%; it takes effect instantly.
LanguageData.US.Help.GlobalVolume.Number.Label: Percent Field
LanguageData.US.Help.GlobalVolume.Number.Text: Type a percentage between 0 and 100. Anything parseable applies live as you type; Enter or clicking away only ends editing.
LanguageData.US.Help.Attenuation.Overview: Camera height maps to the audible distance across the 15-65 band: the start point stays locked at 100% and the end at 0%, dragged horizontally into a linear fade. This is RimWorld's camera-height scale, not map-cell distance from the pawn. Quick presets: Conservative 15-65, Balanced 15-50, Radical 15-40; editing the range by hand switches the preset label to Custom.
LanguageData.US.Help.Attenuation.Chart.Label: Attenuation Chart
LanguageData.US.Help.Attenuation.Chart.Text: Drag the two control points horizontally to set where the fade starts and ends; the left point stays at full audibility and the right at zero, kept at least 5 units apart.
LanguageData.US.Help.Attenuation.Presets.Label: Quick Presets
LanguageData.US.Help.Attenuation.Presets.Text: Three mutually exclusive buttons apply a distance range outright - Conservative 15-65, Balanced 15-50, Radical 15-40 - and the chart and status line update with them. Editing the range by hand switches the label to Custom.
LanguageData.US.Help.Attenuation.Status.Label: Preset / Range Read-out
LanguageData.US.Help.Attenuation.Status.Text: Read-only line under the chart: it names the active preset (Custom after a manual drag) and the current distance range. It changes nothing by itself.
LanguageData.US.Help.BasicTuning.Overview: Playback participation, Talking scaling, global activity and the independent Pawn Eat/Select options. Ordinary responses initialize at startup; the current conditions and selected audio still decide whether a response can play.
LanguageData.US.Help.BasicTuning.Egg.Label: Easter Egg Sounds
LanguageData.US.Help.BasicTuning.Egg.Text: When on, Easter egg entries join the normal pool and can be drawn like any other clip; when off, only ordinary entries are eligible.
LanguageData.US.Help.BasicTuning.ScaleCooldown.Label: Time-Speed Scaling
LanguageData.US.Help.BasicTuning.ScaleCooldown.Text: On, cooldowns follow the game's time speed, so two squeaks keep the same real-time spacing at 1x, 2x and 3x. Off, the raw tick cooldowns are used and high speed compresses them. On by default.
LanguageData.US.Help.BasicTuning.ScaleTalking.Label: Talking Scaling
LanguageData.US.Help.BasicTuning.ScaleTalking.Text: Adjusts the ordinary squeaks by the pawn's Talking ability: the lower the ability, the lower the chance an ordinary attempt passes. Actions with their own talking gate are unaffected. On by default.
LanguageData.US.Help.BasicTuning.ScalePopulation.Text: When many US-connected pawns are within earshot, periodic squeaks thin out: the intervals lengthen and the probability of a random squeak attempt passing falls, both in proportion to the audible count divided by ten (the factor is never below one), so a crowded map is not proportionally noisier. On by default.
LanguageData.US.Help.CameraIndicator.Overview: When enabled, a camera readout line appears above the bottom-left date bar, showing camera height and view size. Compare it against the distance band in Distance attenuation to judge who is audible at the current zoom. It never marks pawns.
LanguageData.US.Help.CameraIndicator.Toggle.Text: Toggles that camera readout line. It is a viewing aid for the attenuation range and changes no audio itself.
LanguageData.US.Help.Timing.Overview: Shows the actual ordinary or explicit development plan. Ordinary state waits start at 600 game ticks, combining activity, audible population and speed exactly once. Once the world is ready, ordinary automatic states use a stable subject phase: the extra success window is at most about 2 seconds and 20% of the effective wait; the extra retry window is at most about 0.25 seconds and half the base retry. Initial spread remains 600 game ticks. Speed changes affect new schedules; existing waits remain. Action/shared limits and the base retry stay in game ticks, and interaction seconds stay unchanged. Effective author and player overrides still apply.
LanguageData.US.Help.Timing.Interval.Label: Call Interval Master
LanguageData.US.Help.Timing.Interval.Text: The hard floor between any two squeaks, in seconds (the slider moves in game ticks, 60 per second). 1.0x uses the default rhythm; raise it to thin out dense crowds. The default 3.6 s suits most colonies.
LanguageData.US.Help.Timing.Multiplier.Label: Cooldown Multiplier
LanguageData.US.Help.Timing.Multiplier.Text: Scales every action cooldown and the global interval at once: 0.5 halves the wait (twice as chatty), 2.0 doubles it. 1.0 is the authored timing.
LanguageData.US.Help.Diagnostics.Overview: Response diagnostics needs neither developer mode nor detailed logs. Close settings normally to resume play, then search and choose a target inside the diagnostics panel. Start recording, reproduce normally, stop and copy feedback. Start does not require a successful snapshot. Viewing B leaves A recording; Stop applies to the recorded target. The latest 64 settled decisions are retained, with overwrites and missing data marked. Technical fields separate the last decision, current sustained slot and latest maintenance. Sequence counts decisions only; maintenance may end a slot without a new decision. LatestMaintenance is one replaceable observation, not decision history. Audio snapshot numbers identify adopted inputs, not sound resources; end times are observed at the adapter, not native completion times. Details and full fields remain scrollable and selectable. Feedback keeps its allowlist and size limit. Opening alone never records. FL.UiKit geometry reports are separate UI-debug tools.
LanguageData.US.Help.Diagnostics.LoggingAuto.Text: Follows the build: dev builds log in detail, release builds stay quiet. This is the default.
LanguageData.US.Help.Diagnostics.LoggingEnabled.Text: Forces detailed logs on, even in release builds. Response output is limited to 64 attempts per pawn per 60 real seconds and renews automatically. This is not a sound limit. Normal feedback recording works with logging off; leave this off unless detailed logs are needed.
LanguageData.US.Help.Diagnostics.LoggingDisabled.Text: Forces all developer logging off, even in dev builds.
LanguageData.US.Help.Diagnostics.LocalizeDebug.Text: When on, the vanilla debug menu shows Universal Squeaker's debug actions with translated names and categories. Only visible while developer mode is enabled.
LanguageData.US.Help.Diagnostics.LayoutDiagnosis.Text: Developer tool. The status line says whether this window's layout is being captured, and if not, why: a release library package has no layout instrument, and no switch can create one.
LanguageData.US.Help.Diagnostics.LayoutCapture.Text: Records every arranged element of this window - its rect in each coordinate space, its height mode and resolved height. Costs frames while on, and is off by default; it is never saved.
LanguageData.US.Help.Diagnostics.LayoutOutline.Text: Draws an outline around the rects this window paints, so a rect can be seen rather than read. It is independent of capture (SA1.5): with capture on it outlines the retained set, with capture off it outlines every drawn rect and samples nothing - no report is armed by this switch.
LanguageData.US.Help.Diagnostics.LayoutReport.Text: Writes the last completed capture once to the log, then stops. Press it again for another. For a rect that does not respond to clicks, read the input lines: each one carries the pointer, the queried rect and the verdict (hit, miss, covered or disabled).
LanguageData.US.Help.ScopeTree.Overview: Choose a general Pawn, Race or legal Xenotype profile, then an action. This page shows effective values and where they came from. Unset fields inherit; explicit No and zero override. Behaviour sources, audio packs and preset imports are separate actions.
LanguageData.US.Help.ScopeTree.Layer.Text: Choose which layer the edits below write to: Global, Race or Xenotype. Layer records stack and resolve one after another.
LanguageData.US.Help.ScopeTree.Domain.Text: On the Race and Xenotype layers, pick the exact race domain - or the (race, xenotype) domain - being edited; the row is hidden on the Global layer.
LanguageData.US.Help.ScopeTree.ActionScope.Text: One dropdown per action: Auto inherits the effective value from below, or force Off, Any or Command within what the action supports. On wide layouts the row shows the effective value with an arrow for inherited scopes.
LanguageData.US.Help.ScopeTree.MoodTuning.Text: Four mood rows - Good, Neutral, Bad, Break - each adjusting pitch, volume and jitter via stepper and number field. Each row ends with two controls: "Reset to default" clears this layer's three factors (the preset source is kept) and "Reset to preset" re-applies that preset's baseline for this row. An unavailable control is still drawn, only disabled - hover it for the reason.
LanguageData.US.Help.ScopeTree.ResetDefault.Text: Removes the exact selected player row, including its template reset target. Author contributions and parent layers remain intact. This differs from clearing only the scope field.
LanguageData.US.Help.ScopeTree.ResetPreset.Text: Re-applies the current template's present fields to this exact player row; unrelated player fields remain. The stored template identity is a reset target, not author-source provenance.
LanguageData.US.Help.ScopeTree.Auto.Label: Auto / Use inherited value
LanguageData.US.Help.ScopeTree.Auto.Text: Inherit clears only this layer's scope field. Other player fields and the template reset target remain; the effective scope then comes from the remaining layers and canonical contract.
LanguageData.US.Help.PresetList.Overview: Templates import sparse values into explicitly selected player layers. They do not bind or replace an author behavior source. A stored template identity provides a separate reset target.
LanguageData.US.Help.PresetList.Tree.Label: Preset Tree
LanguageData.US.Help.PresetList.Tree.Text: Click a preset header to expand its race and xenotype tree and tick the domains that should receive the baseline. Xenotype rows are tagged "(inherits race)" or "(own only)"; the header summary counts the ticks live.
LanguageData.US.Help.PresetList.Import.Text: Applies only template-present fields to the selected exact player domains. Repeating the import does not duplicate rows; values omitted by the template preserve the player's existing fields.
LanguageData.US.Help.FilterBar.Overview: The default range is humanlike, with HAR first; animals, other races and all targets remain reachable. Search, author, Race, Xenotype and state compose over exact pack/domain rows. Collapsing keeps the range, active conditions, matching-pack count and local Clear visible. Queries do not change editing or selections.
LanguageData.US.Help.FilterBar.Keyword.Label: Keyword
LanguageData.US.Help.FilterBar.Keyword.Text: Case-insensitive substring matching covers target names and identities in the target list; in the pack list it covers pack label, DefName, mod, author, key and provided domains. Open a matching pack to inspect its individual targets. Category, source and coverage filters still apply; search never changes selections or the editing domain.
LanguageData.US.Help.FilterBar.Domain.Label: Domain Filter Chips
LanguageData.US.Help.FilterBar.Domain.Text: Enabled, conflict and missing-selection conditions compose. Turning a row off updates its switch immediately; Enabled-only retains the row until Refresh or a query change. Default filters clears this page and returns to humanlike, retaining the viewed pack, editing target, pack selections and behavior source.
LanguageData.US.Help.FilterBar.Author.Text: Expand author candidates to search and page, with at most eight per page. Typing selects nothing. Clicking a candidate filters packs; wrapped display never changes the complete author value. Undeclared authors use the pack source name. Matching remains case-insensitive containment.
LanguageData.US.Help.FilterBar.Race.Text: Choosing a candidate filters to that race and its real xenotype supply. Races without packs remain available and are identified as such. Candidate search and paging do not switch the editing domain. Clearing candidate search is separate from clearing the Race condition.
LanguageData.US.Help.FilterBar.Xenotype.Text: Without a Race condition, each Xenotype Def appears once and lists its real supplying parent domains. With Race set, results use that exact combination. Packless xenotypes remain; an unknown parent never becomes Human. Typing selects no first item. A Xenotype condition excludes race-only rows.
LanguageData.US.Help.FilterBar.Summary.Label: Condition Echo
LanguageData.US.Help.FilterBar.Summary.Text: Shows the category, source and coverage conditions, with matching results against the eligible inventory in that category before paging. These are separate from the global selected-pack/catalog totals. The keyword remains in its field instead of a duplicate label. Clear resets only this list's query and conditions to humanlike; it retains the viewed objects, selections and editing domain.
LanguageData.US.Help.PackCards.Overview: Browse independent packs and inspect exact Race or legal Race/Xenotype targets. A single target has a direct switch; multi-target packs expose separate switches in detail. Selecting one target never enables every target.
LanguageData.US.Help.PackCards.Card.Label: Pack Card
LanguageData.US.Help.PackCards.Card.Text: The pack name sits beside Contents and each exact target sits beside its switch. Only namesakes, exceptional states or multiple targets need extra list identity. Full source, author, DefName and mapped-action count belong in detail. A mapping is not native sound or listening evidence.
LanguageData.US.Help.PackCards.Expand.Text: View only the named pack, without selecting its first domain. Wide layout retains list and detail; compact Back and that layer's Escape retain the viewed identity, query and position. Filtering out a pack preserves its real details. Only explicit domain selection changes the editing target.
LanguageData.US.Help.PackCards.Row.Label: Domain Row
LanguageData.US.Help.PackCards.Row.Text: Choose an exact domain as the context for behaviour or fallback tools. The row switch independently selects only this pack in this domain. Labels are presentation; identity remains pack key plus exact domain.
LanguageData.US.Help.PackCards.Enable.Label: Enable Switch
LanguageData.US.Help.PackCards.Enable.Text: Enables or disables this pack for this domain only. Two rows of one pack are two separate selections; filtering and expanding never write them.
LanguageData.US.Help.Checklist.Overview: The operation domain's status banners: dormant, target not loaded and conflict notices, plus the stale-selection banner with its Forget dangling button.
LanguageData.US.Help.Checklist.Forget.Text: Removes the saved selections whose pack keys are no longer installed; the button appears only inside the stale-selection banner and affects the current domain only.
LanguageData.US.Diagnostics.Pending.SourceMissing: the current source supplied no determination
LanguageData.US.Diagnostics.Na.NoTimingAction: there is no current timing action
LanguageData.US.Diagnostics.Na.ExternalPlanOnly: this gate applies to external trigger plans only
LanguageData.US.Diagnostics.Na.NoScopeMatch: the action's scope is not an active command
LanguageData.US.Diagnostics.Na.GlobalIgnored: the action ignores the global cooldown
LanguageData.US.Diagnostics.Na.NoEvaluationForAction: no completed evaluation for the current action in this session
LanguageData.US.Diagnostics.Na.NoDispatchOutcome: the last evaluation did not reach dispatch
LanguageData.US.Diagnostics.Summary.NoCurrentBlock: No block found in current observations
LanguageData.US.Diagnostics.Previous.NoEvaluation: No evaluation recorded in this session
LanguageData.US.Diagnostics.Previous.NoDispatch: No dispatch recorded in this session
LanguageData.US.Diagnostics.Previous.None: No previous evaluation or dispatch recorded in this session
LanguageData.US.Diagnostics.Recency.JustNow: at {0}, less than a minute ago
LanguageData.US.Preset.List.BaselineNote: Read-only baselines. Apply writes to the checked domains; view and adjust current values on Tuning.
LanguageData.US.Reset.RestoreAll.Caption: Restores player settings, pack selections and all action overrides. Explicit author-source choices, their last-good snapshots and final-fallback tables are kept.
LanguageData.US.Reset.RestoreAll.Confirm: Restore player settings to defaults: output volume and distance, activity, talking scaling, eggs, camera indicator, appearance and entry preferences, diagnostics, pack selections, and every action override with its preset anchor. KEPT: explicit author-source choices and last-good snapshots, final-fallback player tables and sound mappings, author/Def content, and schema/migration diagnostics. This cannot be undone from this window.
LanguageData.US.Reset.Area.Distance.Confirm: This restores the distance area to defaults: output volume, distance preset and the distance range. Action/mood tuning, pack selection and fallback tables are kept.
LanguageData.US.Reset.Area.Basics.Confirm: Restore activity, talking scaling, eggs, camera indicator, and Pawn service-profile Select eligibility and Eat parameters. Race/Xenotype overrides, author-source choices and other settings are kept.
LanguageData.US.Reset.Area.Timing.Confirm: This restores the trigger-timing area to defaults: the minimum interval and the global cooldown multiplier. Other areas and fallback tables are kept.
LanguageData.US.Reset.Area.Diagnostics.Confirm: This restores the diagnostics area to defaults: the developer log mode and the localized debug-action menu. The per-window layout-diagnosis switches are not settings and are untouched.
LanguageData.US.Reset.Area.Action.Confirm: Remove EVERY player action override in the layer/domain shown below, including response parameters, participation and row preset anchors. Values inherit again from the adopted author source and service defaults. Other layers, domains, author-source choices and final-fallback tables are kept.
LanguageData.US.Reset.Area.Mood.Confirm: This restores EVERY mood row of the current layer/domain shown below to defaults (pitch, volume and jitter plus their preset anchors). Other layers, domains and areas are kept.
LanguageData.US.Help.ResetCenter.Overview: Use the global restore to clear player settings, pack selections and action overrides together. Explicit author-source choices, their last-good snapshots and final-fallback player tables remain in place.
LanguageData.US.Help.ResetCenter.RestoreAll.Text: The global restore resets ordinary player settings and removes every action override and its preset anchor. It keeps explicit author-source choices and last-good snapshots, final-fallback tables, author/Def content and schema/migration diagnostics. The existing owner publishes and queues persistence; cancel writes nothing.
LanguageData.US.Help.ResetArea.Overview: Each area carries its own restore: the question lists exactly the fields the area writes and names what stays untouched. Simple restores (the distance preset and range, a single action row) execute directly without a question.
LanguageData.US.Help.ResetArea.Button.Text: Each confirmation names the fields its existing owner resets. Playback behaviour also includes the camera indicator and Pawn service-profile Select/Eat fields. Action-area restore removes every player action override in the named layer/domain, not its explicit author-source choice. Distance defaults resets only the preset and range; distance-area restore also resets output volume. Final-fallback tables are kept.
LanguageData.US.Nav.Advanced.Label: Advanced
LanguageData.US.Page.Advanced.Title: Advanced and diagnostics
LanguageData.US.Page.Advanced.Caption: Developer tools, the global restore and the surface theme, kept off the player pages.
LanguageData.US.Intro.Body: Find the race you want to hear, open its row to the packs page, and switch a pack on there; or use a card's Enable button when a race has exactly one pack to turn on. Nothing plays until a source exists.
LanguageData.US.Help.RaceBoard.Group.Text: The default scope contains humanlike races and legal xenotypes. Races only and Xenotypes only keep those identities separate. Animals and other life kinds require an explicit scope; HAR affects sorting, not admission. All shows the complete legal directory. Browsing never changes audio settings.
LanguageData.US.Help.RaceBoard.Filters.Text: Keyword, life category and actual Def source package act together. Source names are readable; package IDs distinguish namesakes. Search and page the source list; Clear returns this list to its own default. Each list keeps independent filters.
LanguageData.US.Help.RaceBoard.Search.Text: Matches the display name, the def name or the source package of the directory rows. Display only - it changes no selection and no sound.
LanguageData.US.Help.RaceBoard.Counts.Text: The count shows all matching results against the complete eligible inventory, before the bounded result page. Previous and Next reach every matching item. Filtering and paging do not select or write settings.
LanguageData.US.Help.RaceBoard.XenoDir.Text: Xenotypes come from their own loaded Def source, not their genes or voice pack. The default includes legal targets; Xenotypes only contains no Race rows. Without Biotech there are no legal xenotype targets.
LanguageData.US.Help.RaceBoard.XenoRow.Text: One loaded xenotype: its source and how many packs name exactly this target. Open jumps to the audio-packs page filtered to it - with an honest empty result when no pack exists. A single unambiguous pack offers Enable, the same exact write as the packs page.
LanguageData.US.Theme.Note: Colours only. Choosing a palette repaints the page and never moves a control, resets the scroll or changes the sound.
LanguageData.US.Theme.Core.Label: Original dark
LanguageData.US.Theme.Royalty.Label: Royalty
LanguageData.US.Theme.Core.Note: Deep charcoal, pale text and restrained gold actions. Colour changes affect only US; warning, error and disabled states keep distinct roles.
LanguageData.US.Theme.Royalty.Note: Night-blue space carrying gold actions and a dark wine-red selected plate; the series keeps its warm-gold identity, set off by cool blue.
LanguageData.US.Help.Intro.Overview: The one-time teaching. It stays out of the way once collapsed and is a single press from returning.
LanguageData.US.Help.Intro.Collapse.Text: Collapsing hides only this teaching band - the board below stays. The preference is saved with the settings, changes no sound, and the global restore returns it to the open default.
LanguageData.US.Help.RaceBoard.Overview: A read-only board of every loaded race - pack supply, what is selected, the final fallback and why anything is absent. It never claims a sound already played.
LanguageData.US.Help.RaceBoard.Row.Label: Race card
LanguageData.US.Help.RaceBoard.Row.Text: Open jumps to the audio-packs page with the race named and any filter that would hide it cleared; it writes no selection. A card with one exact pack offers Enable, which is the same per-domain write as that page's own switch.
LanguageData.US.Help.RaceBoard.Summary.Label: Board shortcuts
LanguageData.US.Help.RaceBoard.Summary.Text: The output-volume and listen-distance cards jump to this page's own controls - scroll only, they change no setting.
LanguageData.US.Help.RaceBoard.Enable.Text: Only a race with exactly ONE not-yet-enabled pack offers this button, and the button names that exact pack - plus its xenotype target when the scope is Xenotype. The press is the same action as the audio-packs row's own switch, on that exact domain identity; it never changes the sound-source mode. Anything wider shows only Open.
LanguageData.US.Help.FallbackEditor.Overview: The per-race final fallback table: maintainer rows with your overrides, an explicit no-sound marker and restore-inheritance are three different states, shown apart.
LanguageData.US.Help.FallbackEditor.States.Label: Entry states
LanguageData.US.Help.FallbackEditor.States.Text: Override marks a sound you set; Maintainer is the shipped row; NoSound is the silence you chose and Unset follows future updates. Escape clears the selected entry, then the selected race - it never writes a setting.
LanguageData.US.Help.Theme.Overview: Choose Original dark (default), Royalty or Black & gold from the dropdown. The three palettes share one embedded named-role colour resource and affect only US.
LanguageData.US.Help.Theme.Switch.Label: Palette
LanguageData.US.Help.Theme.Switch.Text: Changing the palette repaints colours without moving controls, focus, scroll or drafts. The choice is saved; Restore defaults returns to Original dark. Older removed DLC choices repair to Original dark on loading.
LanguageData.US.Kernel.PolicyRequired: The response runtime is not ready. You can still choose packs and edit settings; check diagnostics for unavailable prerequisites.
LanguageData.US.Kernel.CandidateActive: An explicitly enabled development playback plan is active, not an ordinary default. Sound still depends on the response conditions.
LanguageData.US.Kernel.ResponseEditorRetired: The old probability and mood-factor editors are retired. Action permissions above still apply. Configure independent response enablement, parameters and Apply/Skip participation through the current author/Config contract.
LanguageData.US.Help.BasicTuning.EatDrug.Label: Drug filter
LanguageData.US.Help.BasicTuning.EatDrug.Text: Filters the actual ingested item by IsDrug, independently of nutrition and phase. Any does not require this fact. Default: Any.
LanguageData.US.Help.BasicTuning.EatNutrition.Label: Nutrition filter
LanguageData.US.Help.BasicTuning.EatNutrition.Text: Filters the actual ingested item by IsNutritionGivingIngestible, independently of phase and drug status. Any does not require this fact. Default: Any.
LanguageData.US.Help.BasicTuning.EatPhase.Label: Eat phase
LanguageData.US.Help.BasicTuning.EatPhase.Text: Edits the selected Pawn, Race or Xenotype tuning layer. Whole process includes preparation; execution requires actual chewing or lighting entry. Missing precise facts pause this path, never widen it. Inherit clears only this field.
LanguageData.US.Help.Select.Label: Selection qualifications
LanguageData.US.Help.Select.Text: Official Pawn Select requires player control, awake and not downed by default. Adjust each qualification independently for the current Pawn profile, Race or Xenotype layer; Inherit clears only that layer's field. A response still requires an accepted selection with feedback for the final selected subject. Basics restore clears only the Pawn-profile fields; restore the exact action row to clear Race or Xenotype overrides.
LanguageData.US.Response.Profile: Effective system configuration: volume {0}; activity {1}; audio mode {2}; policy {3}. Select a contract in Actions to inspect the same parameters, dependencies and origins used by the response core.
LanguageData.US.Preset.Invalid: This template is invalid. No settings were changed. See the named preset diagnostic.
LanguageData.US.Help.ScopeTree.ResponseDetails.Text: Read the selected action's current folded values, response participation, parameters, sources and dependencies. These are configuration facts, not a prediction that audio will dispatch.
LanguageData.US.UI.StableFilter: Enabled filter retains these rows while you edit. Refresh or change a filter to recalculate.
LanguageData.US.UI.ChoosePackNote: View a pack from the list, or choose a target from the directory.
LanguageData.US.UI.SelectedForDomain: Use this pack for this target
LanguageData.US.UI.SelectionNote: Viewing is not selection. Target switches show pack selection; playback still depends on its conditions.
LanguageData.US.UI.ToolsNote: Choose what to adjust. Switch tools directly; returning to Voices keeps your pack, target and list position.
LanguageData.US.UI.PresetNote: Choose import targets and review the affected rows. Import changes player overrides, not behaviour-source selection or voice-pack selection.
LanguageData.US.UI.EntryNote: These switches change entry visibility only. Mod Settings remains available; the open panel and playback policy are unaffected.
LanguageData.US.UI.RestoreNote: Prefer the current scope or a single area. Global restore affects all settings and requires confirmation.
LanguageData.US.UI.HelpPinned: Help stays below this page. Close it to regain the space; your page, edits and list position stay put.
LanguageData.US.UI.SourceNote: Choose a Race or legal Xenotype, then its behaviour source. This does not change audio packs or import a preset.
LanguageData.US.UI.SourceChooseDomain: The Pawn profile has no author-source binding. Select a Race or legal Xenotype to change a source.
LanguageData.US.UI.SourceCommitted: Changes saved and applied to subsequent responses.
LanguageData.US.UI.SourcePublishFailed: Changes are saved but could not be applied to playback. Check Diagnostics; do not save the same change again.
LanguageData.US.UI.SourceRejected: This change could not be saved; the previous configuration was not replaced. Check Diagnostics.
LanguageData.US.UI.ObservationBoundary: Policy and save state are real configuration observations. Geometry diagnostics depend on the build; local harness results do not verify game rendering, real Config or audible playback.
LanguageData.US.UI.MissingSelections: Missing saved selections (kept, not counted as selected catalog packs)
LanguageData.US.UI.SparseNote: These values affect only the current action and target. Blank inherits; No and zero are explicit settings. Other fields are kept.
LanguageData.US.UI.RowInvalid: This edit was not saved. Enter a valid number with a decimal point, or leave blank to inherit.
LanguageData.US.UI.SourceTimingRejected: Source timing rejected — select Inherit, or reselect an updated source to commit recovery for this domain only
LanguageData.US.UI.IntervalByOpportunity: Choose the opportunity in the interval editor
LanguageData.US.UI.OutputContext: Change scope / per-action volume and pitch…
LanguageData.US.UI.Help.Field.talking: Controls participation in the defined talking modulation for this action. No explicitly opts out; blank inherits.
LanguageData.US.UI.Help.Field.enabled: Controls whether this action is enabled for this target. Inherit uses the upper layer; No explicitly disables it. Enabled does not guarantee a trigger or sound.
LanguageData.US.UI.Help.Fields.Overview: Check the action and target. Blank inherits; an explicit No or zero does not. Editing one field keeps the others.
LanguageData.US.UI.Help.Field.volume: Volume multiplier for this action and target. Zero mutes; blank inherits. It does not replace the system volume on Voices.
LanguageData.US.UI.Help.Field.pitch: Pitch multiplier for this action and target. Blank inherits; the value must satisfy the parameter range.
LanguageData.US.UI.Help.Source.Text: Check the Race/Xenotype being edited. A source supplies author behaviour configuration for that target, separately from audio packs, player overrides and preset imports. Inherit does not automatically select a lone candidate. A save failure keeps the previous configuration; a saved-but-not-applied result should be checked in Diagnostics without saving the same change again.
LanguageData.US.UI.Help.Field.age: Controls declared age responses for this action. It does not create age responses that an author has not defined.
LanguageData.US.UI.Help.Field.mood: Controls declared mood responses for this action. It does not add mood responses that an author has not defined.
LanguageData.US.UI.Help.Field.interval: Minimum action interval for simulation opportunities, in game ticks. It never gates accepted interactions. A custom contract consuming both types has one interval for each type; the opportunity chooser only changes which value you edit, not the contract or runtime clock. Blank inherits at this layer; zero explicitly disables this interval. Edits do not clear reserved deadlines. Unsupported old hardIntervalTicks records are rejected: explicitly reset or replace the named row/source using the new unit, without converting its number automatically.
LanguageData.US.UI.Help.Field.interaction-seconds: Minimum real seconds between accepted root operations, unaffected by pause or game speed. Ordinary Select defaults to 0.3 seconds; Draft and Undraft each default to 0.6. No additional game-tick action interval applies. Independent or derived contracts own their parameters and default to zero seconds unless explicitly configured. Blank inherits; zero disables this interval. Duplicate or stale roots do not replay; edits do not clear reserved deadlines. Old callers must supply the actual event fact and accepted root/time; no legacy fallback exists.
LanguageData.US.UI.Help.Fields.Title: Settings for this action and target
LanguageData.US.UI.Help.Source.Title: Behaviour sources
LanguageData.US.Activity.Help: Global activity A applies once: future state waits are divided by A; event acceptance is multiplied by A and capped at 1. Hard action/shared limits, eligibility and sound supply remain unchanged. Changing A does not redraw the current wait, reset the owner or clear protection. The default base wait is 600 game ticks (10 seconds at 1x), before population/speed factors. Zero is not Off. Confirm a positive finite value; existing valid values are not clamped to a slider range. Playback defaults restore A to 1.
LanguageData.US.Activity.Invalid: Enter a finite number greater than 0 (for example 0.5, 1 or 2). Use Disabled to turn US off.
LanguageData.US.Activity.Note: 1 is neutral. Higher values shorten future state waits and increase event acceptance; hard limits and response conditions still apply.
LanguageData.US.Activity.Title: Global activity
LanguageData.US.Kernel.ExplicitDevelopmentCandidate: An explicitly selected development plan is active. Sound still depends on the response conditions.
LanguageData.US.Kernel.OrdinaryActive: Ordinary responses are ready. The current mode, selected packs and response conditions determine whether sound can play.
LanguageData.US.Kernel.PolicySelectionRequired: The response runtime is not ready. Pack selection is retained; check diagnostics for unavailable prerequisites.
LanguageData.US.Theme.BlackGold.Note: Near-black surfaces and clear pale text; gold marks actions and selection. Green success, amber warning and red error remain distinct.
LanguageData.US.Theme.BlackGold.Label: Black & gold
LanguageData.US.Browse.HiddenSelection: outside this result page; editing target retained
LanguageData.US.Diagnostics.Capture.NoMap: Enter a map to observe responses.
LanguageData.US.Diagnostics.Capture.EntryHint: After opening, close settings normally to resume play with the diagnostic bar. Opening does not record.
LanguageData.US.Diagnostics.Capture.Copied: Feedback copied. Paste it for the maintainer with a description of the problem.
LanguageData.US.Diagnostics.Capture.CopyFailed: Copy not confirmed ({0}); evidence is retained. You can try copying again.
LanguageData.US.Diagnostics.Capture.Unavailable: This read-only source does not provide capture controls.
LanguageData.US.Diagnostics.Capture.SearchTruncated: Search shows the first 64 matches; more exist. Narrow the query.
LanguageData.US.Diagnostics.Capture.ReadBasis: Saved facts only, not eligibility for the next response. Last successful read: {0} realtime seconds; failures {1} {2}
LanguageData.US.Browse.NoMatches: No matching results. Clear this query or adjust its conditions.
LanguageData.US.UI.PackUnavailable: Pack not loaded; viewing identity retained
LanguageData.US.UI.TargetNoPacks: No VoicePack serves this exact target. The editing target and saved selections are retained.
LanguageData.US.UI.TargetFiltered: This target has supply, but the current conditions do not match. Clear this page's filters.
LanguageData.US.UI.BiotechOff: Biotech is inactive; xenotype selections are retained and currently unavailable.
LanguageData.US.VF1.TargetNeedsTable: This target has no fallback table. Select the candidate below and explicitly create it; sound selection is unavailable until then.
LanguageData.US.Diagnostics.Search.Viewport: Tracked targets in the current viewport
LanguageData.US.Packs.Checklist.RaceUnavailableBanner: This race definition is not loaded. Saved selections are retained for recovery.
LanguageData.US.B.Search: Search names, IDs, packs or sources…
LanguageData.US.B.Kept: Kept until Refresh or a query change
LanguageData.US.B.Loose: Loaded xenotype, no legal race pairing. Browse only; no parent race is assumed.
LanguageData.US.B.UnloadedRace: Race not loaded; saved choices retained
LanguageData.US.B.ChooseTarget: Select a target, or view a pack's contents.
LanguageData.US.B.NoResults: No matching results. Clear these conditions or widen the range.
LanguageData.US.B.NoPackHelp: No pack declares this exact target.
LanguageData.US.B.SupplyCounts: {0} declared packs · {1} selected · {2} selected action mappings
LanguageData.US.B.SupplyRoute.Fallback: Uses the first available layer: exact regular → same-race regular → exact pack fallback → final table.
LanguageData.US.B.SupplyRoute.Remix: Mixes the nonempty supply layers below equally.
LanguageData.US.B.SupplyRoute.Vanilla: Routes only the final table; pack choices are retained.
LanguageData.US.B.ConfiguredOnly: Configuration and mappings only; response eligibility and native sound readiness are evaluated at use.
LanguageData.US.B.VanillaPath: Only the final table is routed; packs are kept.
LanguageData.US.B.RaceRegularOnly: A legal xenotype can borrow only same-race regular supply, never the race pack's PackFallback.
LanguageData.US.B.InvalidTarget: Choose a loaded race or a legal, unambiguous race + xenotype on Voices. No edit is redirected to another target.
LanguageData.US.B.NoAnchor: No preset anchor for this action and layer
LanguageData.US.B.PublicationPending: Saved, runtime publication pending. The existing owner retries automatically; do not save the same change again.
LanguageData.US.B.CreateExplicit: Choose a candidate, then Create. Searching and selection write no table.
LanguageData.US.B.AdmissionNote: New table-only admission requires a full game restart. Already-admitted races use committed mappings at their next legal selection.
LanguageData.US.B.Imported: Imported {0} action rows / {1} fields. Applied now; physical save is queued. Sources and pack choices are unchanged.
LanguageData.US.B.NoLegalDomain: No exact domain is authorized; browse only
LanguageData.US.B.Restore.Applied: Row restored; the ordinary save is queued.
LanguageData.US.B.Help: Targets lists every loaded identity, with HAR humanlike first. Expand a race for its actual xenotype domains. One-pack rows have an exact-target switch; multi-pack rows open independent choices. Packs is a separate browsing lens: Contents does not change the working target. Queries never select a result. Enabled rows remain until Refresh or a query change. Tuning edits the named layer; System contains appearance, diagnostics and restores. The configured path reads declarations, not playback.
LanguageData.US.B.ImportNoChange: No action row imported; no save queued.
LanguageData.US.B.ContributionsHelp: Edit the named action and target only. Blank inherits; No and 0 are explicit values. Response enablement and participation are separate. Parameters keep their original units. Technical details show exact IDs; author parameters use the author's units.
LanguageData.US.B.FieldGroup.Author: Author response settings
LanguageData.US.B.FieldNote.Pitch: Multiplier: 1 is unchanged; must be positive. Blank inherits.
LanguageData.US.B.FieldNote.Volume: Multiplier: 1 is unchanged; 0 is silent. Blank inherits.
LanguageData.US.B.FieldNote.MoodThreshold: A value from 0 to 1, not a percentage. Low must be below High. Blank inherits.
LanguageData.US.B.FieldNote.Jitter: Positive pitch multiplier; maximum must be at least minimum. Blank inherits.
LanguageData.US.B.FieldNote.Participation: Yes applies this response; No skips it. Inherit keeps the upstream choice.
LanguageData.US.B.FieldNote.Response: Enables this declared response, separately from participation. Inherit keeps the upstream choice.
LanguageData.US.B.FieldNote.AuthorParameter: Use the author's parameter units and range. Blank inherits; 0 is an explicit value.
LanguageData.US.Diagnostics.Technical.Seconds: Convert simulation time at 60 ticks per second (not interaction real seconds)
LanguageData.US.B.Help.RosterSearch: Search the current target or voice-pack list by name or identity. Existing category, source and coverage filters still apply. Searching does not choose a target, enable a pack or change the editing domain.
LanguageData.US.B.Help.RosterTargets: Browse loaded targets, including those without voice packs. Open a target to inspect its configured supply; only an explicit toggle changes that exact domain. Biotech and legal Race/Xenotype identity still govern edits.
LanguageData.US.B.Help.RosterPacks: Browse voice packs and open their contents before changing a domain. Viewing a pack does not select an editing target, enable its contents or change the routing mode.
